item.research_question: Can a noble metal-free high entropy glycerate (HEG) composed of five transition metals exhibit superior oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity and stability compared to its binary, ternary, and quaternary subsystems?
item.material_system: FeNiCoCrMn glycerate (HEG) and its subsystems (binary FeNi-G, ternary FeNiCo-G, quaternary FeNiCoCr-G, FeNiCoMn-G, FeCoCrMn-G, FeNiCrMn-G, FeNiCoMn-G, NiCoCrMn-G; unary Fe-G, Ni-G, Co-G)
item.processing_route: Solvothermal synthesis: equimolar metal nitrates (0.5 mmol each of Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Ni) dissolved in isopropanol (34 mL), mixed with glycerol (6 mL), heated in a Teflon-lined autoclave at 150 °C for 10 h, followed by centrifugation, washing with ethanol, and vacuum drying at 60 °C for 24 h
item.test_conditions: 1 m KOH electrolyte; three-electrode system; LSV sweep rate 5 mV s⁻¹; 80% IR compensation; cyclic voltammetry at 100 mV s⁻¹ for 3000 cycles; chronopotentiometry for 36 h at 10 and 100 mA cm⁻²; two-electrode electrolyzer for overall water splitting
key_findings: HEG requires an overpotential of 229 mV to achieve 10 mA cm⁻², outperforming all subsystems.
At 100 mA cm⁻², HEG exhibits the lowest overpotential of 278 mV among all tested glycerates.
HEG displays the lowest Tafel slope of 40 mV dec⁻¹, indicating superior reaction kinetics compared to subsystems (e.g., FeNi-G at 75 mV dec⁻¹).
HEG maintains increased OER activity after 3000 CV cycles, whereas binary, ternary, and quaternary glycerates show decreased activity after 2000 cycles.
The HEG electrolyzer achieves a cell voltage of 1.63 V to reach 10 mA cm⁻² for overall water splitting.
HEG microspheres transform into a porous, amorphous sheet-like structure after OER testing, with uniform metal distribution.
The high entropy configuration results in the highest added high oxidation-state fraction (HOF) and the lowest charge transfer resistance (R_ct).
Removal of Fe from the HEG leads to the worst performance among quaternary subsystems, confirming Fe's critical role.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the enhanced OER activity to synergistic effects where multiple metals modify the electronic structure (increasing Ni³⁺ and Fe³⁺ concentrations) and coordination environment (higher HOF leading to more O—H bonds). The presence of Cr induces strain that weakens chemisorption at active sites. The high entropy configuration promotes amorphization, which provides more active sites with random orientations and unsaturated electronic configurations, accelerating charge transfer. The stability is ascribed to the high entropy configuration effect, which maintains structural integrity during cycling.
item.limitations: The text notes that the exact mechanism for the decrease in charge transfer resistance (R_ct) with M—OH bonding is unknown. It also states that without optimizing the high entropy configuration, the performance is comparable to other reported materials, implying room for further tuning.
item.future_work: The authors propose that further modification of the FeNiCoCrMn-G HEG by adjusting the concentration and/or addition of more metals would lead to optimized glycerates exhibiting superior OER and overall water splitting activities.
quotes: The HEG consists of 5 different metals of Fe, Ni, Co, Cr, and Mn.
The unique glycerate structure exhibits an excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity with a low overpotential of 229 and 278 mV at current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2, respectively.
The excellent catalytic activity is attributed to the synergistic effects; while the excellent electrochemical stability is ascribed to the high entropy configuration.
